install_tell: redis-sentinel /etc/redis-sentinel.conf (port 26379) or redis-server --cluster-enabled yes (cluster bus on data-port+10000, e.g. 16379 for a 6379 node) -- distinct role from the already-tracked 'redis-vector' (RedisSearch/RediStack vector-store use case) and generic cache deployments
misconfig_patterns: Sentinel historically ships with no requirepass -- SENTINEL commands (masters, replicas, get-master-addr-by-name) readable unauth on 26379
Cluster bus port (data-port + 10000) is a separate binary-gossip-protocol listener, rarely firewalled independently of the main data port

SOFT SIGNAL ONLY (per dispatch scope) -- a bare 6379 Redis instance is not inherently 'coordination role'; classify as coordination-candidate only on: (a) a paired 26379 Sentinel on the same host/subnet, (b) CLUSTER INFO returning cluster_enabled:1, or (c) key namespace scan showing lock:/leader:/election:/lease: prefixed keys -- flag, do not force-classify

app-specific coordination keys (e.g. Redlock-pattern lock keys, Bull/BullMQ queue leader keys, Zookeeper-replacement libraries using Redis for leader election) are invisible to a port/banner scan and require a KEYS/SCAN pattern probe -- out of scope for this harvest-only phase, flagged for the scan-phase agent

active_probe.false_positive_check: SENTINEL masters over raw RESP protocol on 26379 returning a monitored-master array (vs error/empty) confirms coordination role directly and unambiguously -- this is the hard fingerprint the soft 6379-only signal cannot provide

deployment_tells: port 26379 open + RESP PING replies +PONG unauth -- Sentinel confirmed
port 16379 (or data-port+10000) open alongside 6379 -- cluster bus, strong cluster-mode signal
6379 INFO replication showing role:master with multiple connected_slaves + a paired 26379 -- HA topology, coordination-adjacent even if not pure metadata store
6379-only with no 26379/cluster-bus and no lock-namespace keys -- do NOT classify as coordination role, route to cache/vector categories instead
pivot_paths: SENTINEL get-master-addr-by-name <name> -> live master IP:port -> pivots directly to the primary data node behind the HA pair
SENTINEL masters -> monitored master group names -> often leak application/service naming convention (attribution signal)
CLUSTER NODES (if cluster-bus reachable) -> full ring topology, all node IP:ports in one unauth call
vulnerabilities: CVE-2025-49844 (RediShell, CVSS 10.0) -- core Redis RCE, applies equally to coordination-role instances, cross-reference with 'redis-vector' entry
